motif: The Ark — A Vessel by Measure
summary: The vessel that did it, as the text specifies it: 300 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high; compartments; pitch inside and outside; an opening near the roof; a door in the side; three decks. The 6-to-1 ratio gives the illustration its long form, and the design floats. What it carried is the point of it: every kind, two by two and seven by seven, brought through uncorrupted; then raven, then dove; then an altar, and a covenant made with every living creature, with the bow as its sign. The text does not specify a prow, keel, rudder or exact joinery, so those remain reconstruction. A boat-shaped hill in Turkey is being drilled as you read this; the evidence lens carries it as a live question.

sources.quote: Noah is told to build an ark of gopher wood, divide it into rooms, and coat it with pitch inside and out. Its dimensions are 300 cubits in length, 50 in width, and 30 in height. It has an opening near the roof, a side door, and lower, middle, and upper decks.
sources.translation: Faithful summary; the wood species and wording of the roof or opening are debated.
sources.notes: The numbers yield a length-to-width ratio of 6:1 and a length-to-height ratio of 10:1. Genesis specifies the overall measurements, not the shape of the ends or the framing method. The squared paper-theatre image is one restrained way to visualize the dimensions, not a recovered plan.

sources.quote: Noah, his household, and living creatures enter the ark. The door is shut; the waters rise and the ark floats. After the waters recede, Noah opens the ark’s window and sends out birds to test whether land has reappeared.
sources.notes: The narrative describes the ark as a vessel of preservation and gives its voyage sequence. It does not describe sails, oars, or steering gear.

sources.textRecorded: surviving Nippur tablet, c. 17th c. BCE
sources.provenance: Fragmentary Sumerian clay tablet from Nippur.
sources.quote: After a destructive flood and storm lasting seven days and nights, a huge boat has been rocked by wind and waves. Ziusudra opens an aperture in it when the sun returns, then offers sacrifice.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.notes: The tablet is broken. It attests a huge boat but does not preserve a complete construction plan.

sources.work: Atrahasis, the Middle Babylonian Ark Tablet
sources.provenance: Akkadian tablets; a Middle Babylonian ark fragment also survives.
sources.quote: A divine warning tells Atrahasis to leave his house and build a boat. Its plan is circular, with equal length and breadth; the account describes ribs, cabins above and below, and bitumen applied to its outer and inner surfaces.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.citation: Middle Babylonian Ark Tablet, lines 1–20; Sources of Early Akkadian Literature edition.
sources.notes: This cuneiform account supplies an actual round-vessel design. Its plan differs sharply from the long 6-to-1 proportions in Genesis.

sources.provenance: Cuneiform copies include tablets from Ashurbanipal’s library at Nineveh.
sources.quote: Ea tells Utnapishtim to build a ship and preserve living things. He loads it, seals its door, survives the storm, grounds it on a mountain, and releases birds to test the waters.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.notes: The ship is given proportions in this account, but they differ from Genesis’s long, narrow 300-by-50-by-30-cubit ark.

sources.textRecorded: text compiled in the 1st millennium BCE
sources.quote: A fish warns Manu of the coming flood and tells him to prepare a ship. When the waters rise, Manu boards; the fish draws the ship by a rope to a northern mountain, where it is fastened as the waters recede.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.notes: The text gives the ship’s role and rope, but no hull dimensions or deck plan.

sources.textRecorded: Apollodorus, Roman era; Ovid, c. 1st c. CE
sources.provenance: Surviving Greek and Latin literary accounts.
sources.quote: Apollodorus says Deucalion makes a provisioned chest on Prometheus’s advice and embarks with Pyrrha. Ovid pictures the pair reaching Mount Parnassus in a small boat.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.notes: Chest and small boat are two literary descriptions of the refuge; neither gives Genesis’s construction specifications.

sources.work: Codex Chimalpopoca, Legend of the Suns
sources.provenance: Nahua-language account preserved in the Codex Chimalpopoca.
sources.quote: Tata and Nene are warned that floodwaters will come. They hollow a cypress log, enter it with food, and survive inside while the world is covered by water.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.citation: Leyenda de los Soles, flood episode in the Codex Chimalpopoca.
sources.notes: The surviving written record is colonial-era; the described refuge is a hollowed log, not a built ship.

sources.textRecorded: recorded by M. Merker, 1904; retold by Frazer, 1918
sources.provenance: Ethnographic transcription and later English retelling.
sources.quote: Tumbainot receives warning, builds a vessel for his family and animals, survives the flood, and sends birds out before leaving it.
sources.translation: Faithful summary of the cited account.
sources.citation: M. Merker, Die Masai (1904); J. G. Frazer, Folk-Lore in the Old Testament, vol. 1, ch. 4 (1918).
sources.notes: A written record of an oral account: Merker wrote it down in 1904 from Maasai elders who, he stated, had not been under missionary teaching. The card gives the date the account was written down; the Maasai gave no date for the story itself, and none is supplied here.

science.intro: The Genesis dimensions can be analyzed as a ship design. The evidence below includes engineering studies of reconstructed vessels and a separate, ongoing investigation of a proposed ark site in Türkiye.

evidence.title: The Korean naval architecture study
evidence.observation: A nine-person team at the Korea Research Institute of Ships and Ocean Engineering compared an ark-proportioned barge with 12 other equal-displacement hull forms. They also tested 1:50 models of three hull forms in a wave tank.
evidence.tie: Their 1994 paper found the ark-proportioned design had high relative safety across structural strength, overturning stability, and motion in waves. It estimated performance in waves above 30 metres under its modeled loading and construction assumptions. The model comparison found a strong safety margin for the design under the conditions studied.
evidence.source: S. W. Hong et al., “Safety Investigation of Noah’s Ark in a Seaway,” Journal of Creation 8(1) (1994), 26–36.
evidence.notes: The team had to assume a barge-type hull, draft, center of gravity, timber thickness, and cargo distribution because Genesis does not specify those details. Their study was supported by the Korea Association of Creation Research.

evidence.title: Why the broad hull resists rolling
evidence.observation: Buoyancy supports a vessel through displaced water. As it heels, the center of buoyancy shifts and can create a restoring moment; low cargo placement and sufficient freeboard also matter.
evidence.tie: Those are the same naval-architecture principles used to evaluate modern ships. Similar principles do not mean modern cruise ships use the ark’s exact hull form or that shape alone guarantees survival.
evidence.source: Texas A&M University College of Engineering, “Floating masterpieces: How engineers design ships to stay afloat” (2021).
evidence.notes: Stability depends on the complete hull, loading, construction, watertightness, and sea conditions, not length and width alone.

evidence.title: Righting after a steep roll
evidence.observation: When a floating vessel tilts, its weight still pulls downward while buoyancy acts upward through a shifted center. Together these forces can turn the vessel back toward upright: the righting couple.
evidence.tie: John D. Morris illustrated an ark cross-section and wrote that this restoring action would right the proposed design from a tilt of up to 90 degrees. That closely matches the steep-roll behavior shown in the simulation described here.
evidence.source: John D. Morris, “The Survival of Noah’s Ark,” Acts & Facts 42(1) (2013), 13.
evidence.notes: The 90-degree statement is Morris’s illustrated stability explanation. The separate 1994 Korean paper reports wave-tank tests and stability calculations; it does not identify this documentary simulation.

evidence.title: Independent buoyancy calculation
evidence.observation: Four University of Leicester physics students applied Archimedes’ principle to the Genesis dimensions, modeling a box-shaped wooden vessel with a stated cubit length and timber density.
evidence.tie: They calculated a theoretical maximum additional load of about 50.54 million kilograms before the model became fully submerged. This is a buoyancy calculation for the assumed hull, separate from the question of how it would behave in waves.
evidence.source: O. Youle, K. Raymer, B. Jordan, and T. Morris, “The animals float two by two, hurrah!” University of Leicester, Journal of Physics Special Topics 12(1) (2013).
evidence.notes: The authors assumed a 48.2 cm cubit, a rectangular hull, 20 cm wooden panels, cypress density, and seawater. Their maximum load corresponds to the hull's full height being submerged, so it is a theoretical upper bound rather than a recommended operating load.

evidence.title: A rectangular-hull stability demonstration
evidence.observation: Harvard’s Natural Sciences Lecture Demonstrations floats differently shaped, loaded model hulls. Its rectangular model develops a stronger restoring force as the center of buoyancy shifts during a roll.
evidence.tie: The demonstration independently illustrates the righting principle relevant to the ark’s broad cross-section. It tests small model hulls, not a replica of the complete Genesis vessel or a 90-degree ark roll.
evidence.source: Harvard University, Natural Sciences Lecture Demonstrations, “Stability in Flotation.”
evidence.notes: In Harvard’s demonstration, the rectangular hull held three one-pound weights on its deck without capsizing; a semicircular comparison hull could not hold one in that arrangement.

evidence.title: A 2026 site investigation in Türkiye
evidence.observation: Sivas Cumhuriyet University, with Noah's Ark Scans, ran the first permitted deep-core season at the boat-shaped Durupınar formation near Doğubayazıt (29 June–11 September 2026): cores to 18 m inside the outline and at control points outside, ground-penetrating radar, resistivity, and about 1,000 soil samples now in a laboratory in Ankara. The August update reported radar anomalies at 3–7 m with regular edges and right-angle intersections, and about 40 percent more carbon in preliminary soil samples from inside than outside. The team's September field report adds organic-rich intervals in the cores, cavities (one that kept refilling with water), a layer at 4–5 m that broke a drill bit, a camera robot that reached about 12 m, and no bedrock or solid limestone met in the interior holes.
evidence.tie: The project director says the carbon analyses of organic matter and any wood will decide, and expects results within months. He called 'proven' headlines misleading in the same breath as describing the data as astonishing. Two field records now stand against each other: the 1988 cores met layered bedrock at 5 m in two holes; the 2026 team reports none in its interior holes. The laboratory work is what can settle it.
evidence.source: Sivas Cumhuriyet University, “Exciting First Results in Our University-Led Noah's Ark Research” (28 August 2026); Noah's Ark Scans field report (23 September 2026); Cenker Atila to NTV and GZT (27 September 2026).
evidence.notes: This is a current field investigation, separate from the vessel-design studies above. Nothing from the 2026 cores has been independently confirmed or published; results are expected in early 2027, with papers and a book on the season planned. The formation's full record — the 1959 discovery, the 1988 drilling, Collins's thin sections, Avcı's geology, the 2023 dating claims and the 2026 season — is kept in the archaeology encyclopedia's Durupınar entry.

evidence.title: A modern full-scale interpretation
evidence.observation: Ark Encounter in Kentucky built a model 510 feet long, 85 feet wide, and 51 feet high, converting Genesis’s cubits using a 20.4-inch royal cubit.
evidence.tie: It helps visitors feel the scale of the design. It is a modern construction and its detailed appearance is an interpretation of the Genesis measurements.
evidence.source: Ark Encounter, “About the Life-Size Noah’s Ark.”
evidence.notes: The Korean study used a shorter 17.5-inch cubit for its engineering model, so its metric dimensions differ while the biblical ratios remain the same.
